attachments.text:
*To Reproduce*

1. Create a non-empty zip file, e.g. xxx.zip
2. Run `vim xxx.zip`
3. Select one entry inside the zip listing and press Enter to open/view it
4. An empty buffer is open. Buffer name is `~/.../zipfile:/.../xxx.zip::xxx.txt`, i.e. with current directory prepended.

*Expected behavior*  
netrw should read the zipped xxx.txt's content into new buffer.

*Environment (please complete the following information):*

• Vim version: from 8.2.3468 (found by git bisect, first bad commit: c6376c798433bcb9ee38a8664299d11454546950) to 8.2.3486 (latest)
• OS: Arch Linux
• Terminal: GNOME Terminal

attachments.text: Since 8.2.3468 (<https://github.com/vim/vim/commit/c6376c798433bcb9ee38a8664299d11454546950|vim/vim@c6376c7>), getting the absolute path of non-existing paths leaks file descriptors. The file descriptor for `fchdir` is left unclosed in specific code path. Steps to reproduce is `:edit notexist/x.txt` and look into `lsof -p $(pgrep vim | tail -n1)`.
